verses.text: So the king and Haman went to dinner with Queen Esther.

On this second day, while they were drinking wine, the king asked Esther again, "What do you want, Queen Esther? It will be given to you. What is your request? Even up to half of my kingdom, it will be done."
Queen Esther answered, "My king, if you are pleased with me, and if it pleases you, please spare my life. This is what I want. And please spare my people. This is what I ask.

My people and I have been sold to be destroyed, killed, and wiped out. If we had only been sold as slaves, men and women, I would have kept quiet. But no enemy could ever make up for the loss this would bring to the king."
King Xerxes asked Queen Esther, "Who is he? Where is the man who dared to do such a thing?"
Esther said, "The enemy and attacker is this evil man Haman!" Then Haman was terrified in front of the king and queen.
The king got up from the wine in a rage and went out into the palace garden. But Haman stayed behind to beg Queen Esther for his life, because he saw that the king had already decided to punish him.

Just as the king came back from the palace garden into the dining hall, Haman was falling on the couch where Esther was lying. The king shouted, "Will he even attack the queen while I am right here in the palace?" As soon as the king said this, servants covered Haman's face.

Then Harbonah, one of the officials serving the king, said, "Look, there is a pole twenty-three meters high standing at Haman's house. He set it up for Mordecai, the man who spoke up to save the king." The king said, "Hang him on it!"
So they hanged Haman on the pole he had set up for Mordecai. Then the king's anger calmed down.
